result.title: Complementary Geometry in Gaussian Splatting
result.summary: Gaussian Splatting has achieved high visual quality in novel view synthesis, but the accuracy of its rendered geometry remains a challenge. In particular, the rendered depth is computed as an opacity-weighted average along each ray, which may not correspond to the actual scene surface. In this paper, we observe that depth predictions from different views of the same frozen Gaussian representation exhibit complementary errors, allowing us to improve novel-view geometry using information from other views without modifying the original representation. Based on this observation, we propose REVEAL, a general framework that selectively refines novel-view depth using complementary geometric information. Specifically, we first reproject depth predictions from source views to the target view and combine them using robust multi-view consensus. We then introduce a learned selection mechanism to determine whether the candidate depth is more accurate than the original prediction, based on the expected reduction in depth error. In addition, we introduce RIG, a real-world benchmark captured with synchronized RGB-D cameras, which provides ground-truth depth for evaluating both static and dynamic reconstruction models. Experiments on 6 Gaussian Splatting backbones across 3 benchmarks show that REVEAL consistently improves depth accuracy while maintaining comparable rendering quality.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 Gaussian Splatting 渲染深度与实际场景表面不符的问题，提出 REVEAL 框架：在冻结的原始表示之外，把源视角深度重投影到目标视角做鲁棒多视图一致性融合，并学习一个选择机制判断候选深度是否比原预测更准确；同时发布带真值深度的 RGB-D 基准 RIG。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不改动内部表示、仅靠外部多视图证据聚合，并由学习到的选择器决定是否采纳候选」的设定，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、旁路修正与采纳/停止决策提供方法线索；但对象是渲染深度而非推理状态，联系需核查。
